title: Adaptive connection pacing and graceful regional holdoff for surge fan-in
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: during cross-region surge events we observe rapid fan-in of connections causing transient KV cache pressure and SLO breaches. This PR adds an adaptive connection pacing layer in the serving runtime plus a regional holdoff coordinator in the control plane to smooth open connection ramps and provide a graceful short-term holdoff when regional ingress spikes are detected. Key goals: avoid wholesale circuit trips, maintain tenant fairness, and keep latency SLOs for high-priority routes. Changes include: pacing algorithm (EWMA-based rate limiter with per-tenant weights), a leaky-window admission smoother for inflight requests, a regional holdoff lease with softbackoff and telemetry-anchored decay, an operator-configurable safety toggle for immediate disable, end-to-end unit+integration tests, and docs for operators. Rollout plan: enabled behind feature flag, gradual canary to 10% of traffic then 50%; metric thresholds documented. Rollback plan: feature flag off or revert the holdoff coordinator; and a targeted emergency circuit unstick script included. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration scenario harness, [x] telemetry dashboards and alerting playbook, [x] k8s helm values, [x] operator docs. Related: ENG-2841 (holdoff design), ENG-2990 (pacing spec).
commits_summary: 7 commits: initial pacing core and interfaces; add telemetry counters and histograms; implement regional holdoff coordinator and lease logic; add e2e harness and stress tests; helm and values for rollout; operator docs and runbook; fix CI flake in pacing_test by reducing timing dependence.
review_comments: Marco Rivera: I like the EWMA approach. Two asks: (1) can we expose a per-tenant max window to avoid cold-start starvation? (2) add a safety clamp when kv-pressure > threshold so we don't amplify congestion.
Aisha Patel: Answered: added tenant_max_window config and a kv_pressure clamp that forces immediate softbackoff. See region_holdoff.go lines 82-110 and new helm value pacing.tenantMaxWindow.
Elena Kim: CI flaked on pacer_test when run under race detector; add a small jitter in test to avoid deterministic timing. Also request a metrics tag for route priority.
Aisha Patel: Addressed: introduced test jitter and added metrics label route_priority to histograms. CI now green.
Trevor Huang: Are we confident this won't create additional request reordering during hedged-retries? Can we opt-out hedging for paced routes?
Aisha Patel: Added opt-out flag hedging.enabledPerRoute=false for paced routes and added a short note in docs explaining tradeoffs.
ci_summary: CI run: build passed, unit tests passed, integration stress scenario passed after fix; one transient lint failure on first run which was fixed in commit 4.
release_notes: Added adaptive connection pacing and a regional holdoff coordinator to mitigate transient inbound surge fan-in. Feature is behind a feature flag and off by default. Operators can enable gradual rollout via helm values. New telemetry: pacing.request_rate, pacing.window_size, holdoff.leases_active. See docs/operational/regional-holdoff.md for runbook.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: runtime changes are guarded by feature flag and per-tenant clamps. Integration stress tests in CI replicate fan-in scenarios. Emergency toggle and rollback documented. Observability added to detect regressions quickly.
notes_on_hotfix: During initial CI runs a timing-sensitive test caused a transient failure under race detector; fixed by adding controlled jitter and a tighter condition in pacer_test. No customer-facing rollback required during merge window.
